question: Who authored the book "Careless People: A Cautionary Tale of Power, Greed, and Lost Idealism" released in March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarah Wynn-Williams**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book titled **"Careless People: A Cautionary Tale of Power, Greed, and Lost Idealism"** is authored by **Sarah Wynn-Williams**, a former high-ranking executive at **Meta Platforms Inc.** (formerly **Facebook**). ***Hence, the correct answer is Sarah Wynn-Williams.***
 
• Released in **March 2025**, the book serves as a **memoir** and a **critical analysis** of the inner workings of one of the world's most powerful **Big Tech** companies during a period of extreme **global controversy**.
 
• **Sarah Wynn-Williams** served as the **Director of Global Public Policy** at **Meta**, where she managed the company's relationships with **governments** and **international organizations** across various continents.
 
• The narrative focuses on the **corporate culture** of **Silicon Valley**, highlighting how the original **mission** of "connecting the world" was allegedly overshadowed by a pursuit of **growth**, **market dominance**, and **profit**.
 
• The book provides an insider's account of the company's response to the **Cambridge Analytica** scandal, the spread of **misinformation**, and the **ethical dilemmas** faced by those within the **policy** and **communications** departments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sheryl Sandberg (Option A):** She is the former **Chief Operating Officer (COO)** of **Meta** and the author of the influential books **"Lean In"** (**2013**) and **"Option B"**. While she is a central figure in the history of **Facebook**, she did not author this **2025** title. ***Hence, Option A is incorrect.***
 
• **Simon Sinek (Option C):** He is a renowned **author** and **motivational speaker** known for books such as **"Start with Why"** and **"The Infinite Game"**. His work generally focuses on **leadership** and **organizational psychology** rather than specific corporate exposés. ***Hence, Option C is incorrect.***
 
• **Boria Majumdar (Option D):** He is a well-known **Indian sports journalist** and **author** who has written extensively on the history of **Indian cricket** and **Olympics**. His literary contributions are unrelated to the **American tech industry**. ***Hence, Option D is incorrect.***
 
• The title **"Careless People"** is a literary reference to **F. Scott Fitzgerald's** classic novel **"The Great Gatsby"**, symbolizing a class of people who use their **power** and **wealth** to cause damage without taking **responsibility** for the consequences.
 
• The book is expected to be a significant resource for **policymakers**, **tech ethics** researchers, and **students** of **corporate governance** globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The book explores the **regulatory challenges** faced by **social media** companies, including the implementation of the **General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)** in the **European Union** and the **Digital Services Act (DSA)**.
 
• It provides **data** and **anecdotes** regarding the **lobbying** efforts of **Big Tech** in **Washington D.C.** and **Brussels**, illustrating the **functions** of a **Global Public Policy** team.
 
• The release coincides with a period of intense **antitrust** investigations into **Meta**, **Google**, and **Amazon** by the **Federal Trade Commission (FTC)** and various **Attorney Generals** in the **USA**.
 
• **Sarah Wynn-Williams** previously worked in **government relations** and **diplomacy**, bringing a unique **international relations** perspective to the **technological** landscape.
